title: A vendor invoice is due by the vendor's term and recalculated on change
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create a new term of the shop's own for this test, term A, due 14 days after the invoice date, so a vendor on it has vendor invoices due 14 days after their date.
  • Create vendor A for this test, on term A, so the new vendor invoice starts on term A.
  • Create vendor B for this test, on Net 30.
  • Start with a new vendor invoice for vendor A open in Parts, Vendors, Vendor Invoices, not yet saved, so its due date follows vendor A's term.
custom_steps:
1. Set the invoice date to Oct 5, 2026.
  2. Save the vendor invoice.
  3. Change the invoice date to Oct 20, 2026.
  4. Save the vendor invoice.
  5. Change the vendor to vendor B.
  6. Save the vendor invoice.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The due date shows Oct 19, 2026 (Oct 5 + 14 days).

Step 2:

  • The vendor invoice is saved with due date Oct 19, 2026.

Step 3:

  • The due date is recalculated to Nov 3, 2026 (Oct 20 + 14 days).

Step 4:

  • The vendor invoice is saved with due date Nov 3, 2026.

Step 5:

  • The due date is recalculated to Nov 19, 2026 (Oct 20 + 30 days, Net 30).

Step 6:

  • The stored due date is Nov 19, 2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Credit terms", Confluence 963346440, version 3 (22 Oct 2026, "Renamed to Credit terms", Chris Ward), read 23 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11638, story SV-11676 (Story 7, Due dates)

  • S7-R9: “A vendor invoice stores no term. Its due date is calculated by the same rules from the vendor's term when the vendor invoice is created, recalculated when its invoice date or its vendor changes, and stored.”
  • S7-R1: “A Net term (standard or the shop's own) is due that many days after the invoice date: an invoice dated Oct 5 on Net 30 is due Nov 4; on a shop's "Net 10" it is due Oct 15.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
